title: Evaluating outputs: metrics, checks and their limits

questions.q: Why is PSNR between two seeds of one prompt no use as a quality score?
options: The two pictures aren't meant to match pixel for pixel
questions.answer: The two pictures aren't meant to match pixel for pixel
questions.why: PSNR measures error from a target. Different seeds have no shared target.

questions.q: Two changes have the same PSNR. What does that tell you?
options: The same mean squared error, not the same kind of damage
questions.answer: The same mean squared error, not the same kind of damage
questions.why: The lab's brighter and noisy rows are both 20.00 dB, with very different SSIM.

questions.q: Why does adding a constant leave Pearson r at 1?
options: It removes each image's mean before comparing
questions.answer: It removes each image's mean before comparing
questions.why: Correlation subtracts means, so a constant shift vanishes.

questions.q: You compare FID of a model at 500 samples with another at 10,000. What's wrong?
options: FID is biased upward at small sample sizes, so they aren't comparable
It should be measured on one image
questions.answer: FID is biased upward at small sample sizes, so they aren't comparable
questions.why: The lab shows FID falling with sample size when the true distance is 0.

questions.q: Which pair fits a pixel metric best?
options: An image and its VAE round trip
questions.answer: An image and its VAE round trip
questions.why: That pair should match, so error is meaningful. This lesson's graph makes one.
